open_points.subject: advance_run trace derivation
open_points.text: derive every element's conclusion from the trace: a function element from its NodeExecution's status
open_points.question: When an element has multiple NodeExecutions, which execution determines its current conclusion?
options: the greatest attempt_number
the last execution in store order
combine all executions according to status precedence
open_points.default_guess: Use the greatest attempt_number.

open_points.subject: advance_run flow wiring
open_points.text: flow inputs delivered along every edge from them
open_points.question: How are flow-input and flow-output endpoints represented when FlowEdge only has from_node and to_node strings and no endpoint kind?
options: reserved node identifiers
port names used as node identifiers
edges describe only node-to-node links and flow endpoints are inferred separately
open_points.default_guess: Treat an endpoint whose identifier is not a node_id as a flow port name.

open_points.subject: advance_run input assembly
open_points.text: a node is ready when every input port holds its value: flow inputs delivered along every edge from them, constants to their port, and outputs of a concluded succeeded node along every edge
open_points.question: What happens when multiple enabled edges or a constant and an edge deliver values to the same input port?
options: reject or fail the node
choose one by graph declaration order
choose one by source identifier order
require equal values
open_points.default_guess: Use graph declaration order and take the first available source.

open_points.subject: advance_run input ordering
open_points.text: given ... inputs: tuple[PortRef, ...]
open_points.question: In what order must a node element's input PortRefs be assembled?
options: target port declaration order
edge and constant declaration order
PortRef port-name order
open_points.default_guess: Use target port declaration order.

open_points.subject: advance_run constants
open_points.text: constants to their port
open_points.question: How is a FlowConstant.value converted into a StoredValue/PortRef, including canonical bytes, schema, disclosure class, identity, persistence, and size checking?
options: constants already refer to stored values
parse and publish constants when first delivered
publish all constants at run start
open_points.default_guess: Parse the value as canonical JSON and publish it when first delivered.

open_points.subject: advance_run guarded edges
open_points.text: whose guard is absent or whose guard port value equals the guard value as canonical JSON text
open_points.question: Which element or input supplies guard_port, and how are its bytes obtained and compared to guard_value?
options: a port of the source node's outputs
a port of the destination node's inputs
a flow input
any currently available port in the run
open_points.default_guess: Treat guard_port as a source-node output port and compare decoded canonical JSON text exactly.

open_points.subject: advance_run guard evaluation
open_points.text: every edge whose guard is absent or whose guard port value equals the guard value
open_points.question: How is an edge classified while its guard port has not yet concluded or is waiting/failed?
options: not yet decidable
disabled
upstream failed
open_points.default_guess: Treat it as not yet decidable until the guard source concludes.

open_points.subject: advance_run skipped nodes
open_points.text: every edge into it is disabled by its guard or comes from a skipped node
open_points.question: What is the result for an input port with no incoming edge and no constant, or for a node with no inputs?
options: missing inputs imply skipped_by_guard
missing inputs imply upstream_failed
the graph is assumed valid and this cannot occur
a zero-input node is ready
open_points.default_guess: Assume graph validity; make a zero-input node ready and treat an unsourced required input as skipped_by_guard.

open_points.subject: advance_run failure propagation
open_points.text: a node with an input from a failed or upstream_failed node concludes upstream_failed, which wins over skipped_by_guard
open_points.question: When an input has several possible sources, does one failed source force upstream_failed even if another enabled source supplies a value?
options: any failed source forces failure
failure only when no viable source remains
the graph forbids multiple sources
open_points.default_guess: Fail only when no viable source remains.

open_points.subject: advance_run operation context
open_points.text: started_under the store_position of the FlowActivation read with ActivationBeforeRun
open_points.question: Which RecordSet field and which record should be used if the ActivationBeforeRun query returns zero or multiple FlowActivations?
options: require exactly one flow_activation
take the greatest store_position
take the first result
open_points.default_guess: Require exactly one flow_activation and raise StoreInternalError otherwise.

open_points.subject: advance_run operation retry
open_points.text: operation elements that wait are not reached again here
open_points.question: If a previous waiting conclusion has ceased to wait because an approval or attempt was decided, should advance_run itself reach the operation again or only continuation/recovery functions do so?
options: advance_run reaches it once the wait is resolved
only the explicit continuation or recovery path reaches it
derive a conclusion without another reach
open_points.default_guess: Only the explicit continuation or recovery path reaches it.

open_points.subject: advance_run operation records
open_points.text: After an operation element, whose concluding record effects wrote, the next RecordRunProgressChange holds the records it made non-executable
open_points.question: After reach_operation_element returns, must the run and complete trace be reread before determining newly non-executable elements, or is the returned conclusion sufficient?
options: reread both run and trace
reread only the trace
use only the returned conclusion
open_points.default_guess: Reread the run and trace.

open_points.subject: advance_run refused execution
open_points.text: If any NodeExecution of the run is refused_by_owner it reaches nothing and ends the run refused
open_points.question: What outputs, waiting points, executions, and ended_at must be placed in the progress change that records the refused terminal state?
options: retain produced outputs and clear waiting
clear outputs and waiting
retain both outputs and unresolved waiting points
open_points.default_guess: Retain already produced outputs, clear waiting points, write no executions, and set ended_at with kernel_now.

open_points.subject: advance_run mapped source
open_points.text: A mapped element receives the list element at its map_index ... or the spooled file at that position
open_points.question: Which PortRef forms and cardinalities are valid for map_over, and how is the map length obtained for a value reference versus a file reference?
options: only many value/file ports may be mapped
any JSON array value or SpooledFilesRef may be mapped
cardinality is ignored and runtime content decides
open_points.default_guess: Require map_over to name a many port; parse a stored JSON array or use the SpooledFilesRef.files length.

open_points.subject: advance_run mapped value elements
open_points.text: receives the list element at its map_index as its own StoredValue of the map_over port's value_schema and the list's class
open_points.question: When and how is each element StoredValue published and recorded, and is its identity derived from the element bytes or inherited from the list?
options: publish and record an element value before executing it
publish it with the element's progress change
use an ephemeral reference without recording a StoredValue
open_points.default_guess: Publish from the element's canonical bytes and include its StoredValue in the same progress change as the element execution.

open_points.subject: advance_run mapped output aggregation
open_points.text: the canonical JSON array of the elements' values in element order
open_points.question: What exact canonical JSON serialization and canonical array-schema serialization must be used?
options: standard json with sorted keys and compact separators
concatenate already canonical element texts inside brackets
an external canonicalization algorithm not provided
open_points.default_guess: Concatenate the canonical element JSON bytes with commas inside brackets and construct a compact sorted-key JSON schema.

open_points.subject: advance_run mapped output aggregation
open_points.text: only a list that is delivered, to a node or a flow output, is measured, and an output no edge takes fails nothing
open_points.question: If the same mapped output has both disabled and potentially enabled consumers, exactly when is it considered delivered and measured?
options: when any enabled edge or flow output consumes it
when any edge exists regardless of its guard
when all guards are resolved
open_points.default_guess: Measure it once an enabled consumer or a flow output requires it, after relevant guards are resolved.

open_points.subject: advance_run mapped output aggregation
open_points.text: every delivered list of a mapped node MUST be measured before any of them is delivered or written, and when one exceeds the ceiling none of them is delivered
open_points.question: How are all mapped outputs precomputed and size-checked atomically when put_value_bytes publishes values individually and provides no rollback?
options: compute all bytes and sizes before any put_value_bytes call
publish then omit records on failure
the store transaction rolls back unpublished values
open_points.default_guess: Compute every aggregate byte string and validate all sizes before publishing any of them.

open_points.subject: advance_run mapped output aggregation
open_points.text: when one exceeds the ceiling none of them is delivered ... counting as failed by the same derivation, with no record of its own
open_points.question: How is this recordless mapped-node failure represented on later calls and distinguished from an aggregate that has not yet been delivered?
options: recompute the oversized condition from element executions every time
write an upstream_failed record for the mapped node despite the note
store an implicit marker elsewhere
open_points.default_guess: Recompute the oversized condition deterministically from element executions whenever deriving state.

open_points.subject: advance_run mapped file outputs
open_points.text: one SpooledFilesRef listing every element's files in element order, derived from the elements' NodeExecutions whenever it is delivered
open_points.question: How are file keys and disclosure classes reconstructed from NodeExecution outputs after restart when NodeExecution stores only PortRefs and the exact ordering of many files must be preserved?
options: read SpooledFile records by keys in each SpooledFilesRef
query all files for the run and sort their keys
the NodeExecution PortRefs contain sufficient ordered keys
open_points.default_guess: Use the ordered keys already contained in each execution's SpooledFilesRef and read file records only when facts are needed.

open_points.subject: advance_run mapped node conclusion
open_points.text: a mapped node concludes only when every element concluded, succeeded only when all succeeded
open_points.question: If elements finish with different failures or waits, which status/detail represents the mapped node for dependency propagation and final run status?
options: first element by map_index
highest-severity status
mapped node has only an aggregate failed/waiting category
open_points.default_guess: Use the first non-success element in map_index order, while allowing waits to keep the aggregate waiting until all elements conclude.

open_points.subject: advance_run empty mapping
open_points.text: writes one NodeExecution succeeded without map_index ... every output an empty list
open_points.question: For an empty mapping, how are one-cardinality outputs represented as empty lists, particularly file outputs and value outputs whose declared schema is not an array?
options: all outputs become aggregate many references
only many outputs are permitted on mapped nodes
construct empty aggregate references regardless of declared cardinality
open_points.default_guess: Treat every mapped output as an aggregate list regardless of the underlying output port cardinality.

open_points.subject: advance_run progress batching
open_points.text: After each function element MUST write one RecordRunProgressChange ... holding that element's execution ... and every skipped_by_guard and upstream_failed record that became determined
open_points.question: Must propagation continue transitively and include all newly determined records in that same change, or only records immediately determined by the just-finished element?
options: include the full transitive closure
include only immediate dependants
include all currently determinable nodes after scanning in node order
open_points.default_guess: Include the full deterministically computed closure of non-executable records.

open_points.subject: advance_run progress batching
open_points.text: holding that element's execution, its StoredValues and SpooledFiles, and every skipped_by_guard and upstream_failed record
open_points.question: Do StoredValues created for mapped input elements or aggregate mapped outputs belong in this change, a later change, or the final change?
options: the change where they are first needed
the producing element's change
the next node's change
open_points.default_guess: Include them in the first progress change in which their references are delivered.

open_points.subject: advance_run cleanup
open_points.text: the files its attempt spooled are discarded with no SpooledFile record naming them
open_points.question: How can files from only the failed attempt be removed when the imports provide spool_file and remove_run_spool but no per-file or per-attempt removal operation?
options: leave unrecorded spool files until whole-run cleanup
remove the entire run spool
spool only after every output has validated
open_points.default_guess: Buffer/validate outputs first and spool last; if a later spool fails, leave unrecorded files for whole-run cleanup.

open_points.subject: advance_run cleanup_failed
open_points.text: with status running and the waiting points unchanged
open_points.question: Which waiting points are 'unchanged' if the in-memory run/trace already reveals resolved waits not reflected in the stored Run?
options: copy run.waiting exactly
rederive current waits from the trace
retain only unrelated waits
open_points.default_guess: Copy run.waiting exactly.

open_points.subject: advance_run finalization
open_points.text: When nothing can execute: if any element waits ... if nothing waits, the run ends succeeded ... and failed otherwise
open_points.question: How are unconcluded nodes in a cycle or with permanently missing inputs classified and recorded when they are neither ready, waiting, skipped_by_guard, nor upstream_failed?
options: end failed without node records
record upstream_failed
raise StoreInternalError for an invalid graph
open_points.default_guess: Raise StoreInternalError because the graph cannot be deterministically progressed.

open_points.subject: advance_run terminal cleanup
open_points.text: ignore its StoreInternalError
open_points.question: Should errors other than StoreInternalError from remove_run_spool propagate, and can remove_run_spool raise any declared alternative?
options: propagate every other exception
ignore every cleanup exception
only StoreInternalError is possible
open_points.default_guess: Catch only StoreInternalError and propagate anything else.

open_points.subject: all validation refusals
open_points.text: raise RefusedError naming its status
open_points.question: What exact RefusedError constructor arguments and message formats must be used for the many requirements that say an error must 'name' a status, port, failed check, or node?
options: free-form human-readable strings
stable machine-readable codes
multiple positional constructor arguments
open_points.default_guess: Use a single concise string containing the named value.

open_points.subject: cancel_run
open_points.text: with ... the produced outputs
open_points.question: Should cancellation copy run.outputs exactly or rederive newly available flow outputs from the latest trace before writing the cancellation change?
options: copy run.outputs
derive all currently produced outputs from the trace
call advance_run first
open_points.default_guess: Copy run.outputs exactly so cancellation sends nothing further.

open_points.subject: capture_failed_execution
open_points.text: the record's inputs as they are — a StoredValuesRef as it is and spooled files as their SpooledFilesRef
open_points.question: Does 'a StoredValuesRef' mean each individual StoredValuesRef in the tuple, or a nonexistent aggregate StoredValuesRef container?
options: pass the tuple of individual PortRefs unchanged
wrap value references in an aggregate object
normalize references before passing
open_points.default_guess: Pass execution.inputs unchanged.

open_points.subject: capture_failed_execution
open_points.text: read the NodeExecution of the AttemptKey with RecordsByAttempt
open_points.question: What should happen if the query returns multiple matching NodeExecutions or a RecordSet with an unexpected cardinality?
options: take the sole record and treat other cardinalities as StoreInternalError
take the last record
take the first record
open_points.default_guess: Require exactly one record; zero means UnknownReferenceError and multiple means StoreInternalError.

open_points.subject: continue_after_approval
open_points.text: After an approve decision MUST reach the approval's element again with reach_operation_element in this request
open_points.question: How are the RunContext and current input PortRefs required by reach_operation_element reconstructed, and which actor is passed?
options: rederive context and inputs from the run graph/trace and pass the caller actor
reuse approval.preview.inputs and derive context
the ApprovalDecision supplies hidden reach data
open_points.default_guess: Rebuild the context and current inputs from the run and pass the caller actor.

open_points.subject: continue_after_approval
open_points.text: After a refuse decision MUST reach nothing and advance the run ... which ends it refused
open_points.question: Must the refusal_record returned by decide_effect_approval be inspected or written here, and what if it is absent or its status is not refused_by_owner?
options: effects already persisted it; validate and rely on the trace
write it through RecordRunProgressChange
ignore the returned record entirely
open_points.default_guess: Assume effects persisted it, validate that it exists for refusal, then let advance_run derive refusal from the trace.

open_points.subject: continue_after_resolution
open_points.text: After a not_applied resolution MUST reach the element again with reach_operation_element
open_points.question: How are the operation element's current inputs, RunContext.started_under, and actor chosen for this reach?
options: rederive them and pass the caller actor
reuse EffectAttempt.inputs and derive the context
resolve_unknown_outcome performs the reach internally
open_points.default_guess: Use EffectAttempt.inputs, derive the activation context, and pass the caller actor.

open_points.subject: derive_run_answer waits
open_points.text: for reason owner_approval, the approval_id that operation_element_conclusion gives
open_points.question: How can derive_run_answer construct the RunContext required by operation_element_conclusion when it is not told to read ActivationBeforeRun, and what happens if that activation is absent?
options: query ActivationBeforeRun inside derive_run_answer
find the approval directly with ApprovalsOfElement
approval_id should already be stored in WaitingPoint
open_points.default_guess: Query ActivationBeforeRun and raise StoreInternalError if it is absent.

open_points.subject: derive_run_answer waits
open_points.text: the approval_id that operation_element_conclusion gives
open_points.question: What should be returned if the conclusion no longer waits, waits for a different reason, or yields no approval_id while the stored WaitingPoint still says owner_approval?
options: use null
omit the stale wait
raise StoreInternalError
open_points.default_guess: Omit the stale wait after rederiving current conclusions.

open_points.subject: derive_run_answer outputs
open_points.text: a ProducedOutput with the value_id for every produced output
open_points.question: How can a produced file output be represented when ProducedOutput has only value_id and no file reference or file identifier field?
options: ProducedOutput applies only to value outputs
put a serialized file-reference identity into value_id
file flow outputs are forbidden but that constraint is unstated
open_points.default_guess: Assume flow outputs are restricted to value carriage and raise StoreInternalError for a produced file output.

open_points.subject: derive_run_answer missing outputs
open_points.text: reason skipped_by_guard when every edge into it was disabled by its guard or comes from a node recorded skipped_by_guard
open_points.question: How is a missing flow output with no incoming edges, multiple mixed sources, or an upstream-failed source classified?
options: not_produced unless all existing sources are guard-skipped
vacuously skipped_by_guard when there are no edges
inherit upstream failure as not_produced
open_points.default_guess: Use skipped_by_guard only when at least one incoming edge exists and all are disabled or skipped; otherwise use not_produced.

open_points.subject: execute_function_element input loading
open_points.text: read every input's bytes with read_value_bytes into PortPayloads by port
open_points.question: How are StoredValuesRef and SpooledFilesRef converted into ByteSource and then into JsonPayload, FilePayload, or FileListPayload, especially for many value inputs?
options: construct StoredValueSource/SpooledFileSource for each reference and payload by target port metadata
read references directly despite the ByteSource contract
query StoredValue/SpooledFile records first
open_points.default_guess: Construct StoredValueSource for values and one SpooledFileSource per file key, then build payloads using the contract port's carriage and cardinality.

open_points.subject: execute_function_element output validation
open_points.text: On succeeded, each JSON output above ... concludes contract_violation ... otherwise JSON outputs are published
open_points.question: Which checks are required for missing, duplicate, extra, wrong-carriage, wrong-cardinality, invalid-schema, noncanonical JSON, media-type, or oversized file outputs from the sandbox?
options: run fit_port_value for every declared output and require exact names
trust execute_function to enforce everything except the stated JSON ceiling
perform only name and size checks
open_points.default_guess: Assume execute_function enforces the output contract except for the explicitly required stored-value ceiling.

open_points.subject: execute_function_element output ordering
open_points.text: the StoredValues and SpooledFiles of its outputs
open_points.question: In what order must output PortRefs, StoredValues, SpooledFiles, and files within many outputs be returned?
options: contract output-port order and list order
SandboxResult.outputs order
port-name order
open_points.default_guess: Use contract output-port order and preserve list order within each port.

open_points.subject: execute_function_element disclosure
open_points.text: highest_disclosure_class gives for the classes of every input value and file the element received
open_points.question: What disclosure class is used for a zero-input function, where highest_disclosure_class would receive an empty tuple?
options: open
the output port's declared disclosure_class
highest_disclosure_class defines an undocumented empty result
open_points.default_guess: Use open.

open_points.subject: execute_function_element disclosure
open_points.text: no output is of a lower class than an input
open_points.question: Should an output's class also be raised to its output port's declared disclosure_class when that class is higher than every input?
options: maximum of input-derived and port-declared class
input-derived class only
port-declared class only
open_points.default_guess: Use the maximum of the input-derived class and any declared output-port class.

open_points.subject: execute_function_element attempt number
open_points.text: the element's next attempt_number — the count of its NodeExecutions read with ExecutionsOfElement plus one
open_points.question: Does the count include every historical execution including derived skipped/upstream records, and how are concurrent attempts prevented from selecting the same number?
options: count all NodeExecutions for the element
count only executions with executed present
use maximum attempt_number plus one
open_points.default_guess: Use the number of all NodeExecutions plus one, assuming run advancement is serialized.

open_points.subject: execute_function_element spool failure
open_points.text: a RefusedError from spool_file concluding resource_exhausted ... no outputs and no file of that attempt kept
open_points.question: If a later spool_file call fails after earlier files were already spooled, how can those earlier files be removed without a per-file removal import?
options: preflight cannot guarantee success; leave them unrecorded until run cleanup
remove the entire run spool
spool_file is assumed atomic across the whole attempt
open_points.default_guess: Leave earlier unrecorded files for whole-run cleanup and return no SpooledFile records.

open_points.subject: execute_function_element storage failure
open_points.text: JSON outputs are published with put_value_bytes
open_points.question: How should put_value_bytes failures be translated, and what happens to values successfully published before a later output fails?
options: propagate store errors
translate RefusedError to resource_exhausted
translate any failure to crashed
open_points.default_guess: Propagate store errors; unpublished record references make earlier blobs unreachable.

open_points.subject: execute_function_element timestamps
open_points.text: take started_at from kernel_now ... ended_at taken when the outcome is built
open_points.question: For post-sandbox publication or spool failures, is ended_at taken immediately after execute_function, after all output validation, or after all publishing/cleanup?
options: after all validation and publication work
immediately when execute_function returns
at the first detected failure
open_points.default_guess: Take ended_at when the final NodeExecutionDraft is constructed after validation and publication attempts.

open_points.subject: recover_running_runs cleanup enumeration
open_points.text: first call remove_run_spool for every run that has ended and keeps no spool
open_points.question: How are all such ended runs obtained when the described RunsByStatus query is only for running, awaiting_approval, and pending runs?
options: issue a separate RunsByStatus query for terminal statuses
read all run records through an unspecified query
cleanup only terminal runs returned incidentally
open_points.default_guess: Issue a separate RunsByStatus query for succeeded, refused, cancelled, and failed, then filter failed by released_by.

open_points.subject: recover_running_runs kernel actor
open_points.text: under an Actor of kind kernel
open_points.question: What agent_name must the kernel Actor carry?
options: null
kernel
the current process or service name
open_points.default_guess: Use agent_name null.

open_points.subject: recover_running_runs lag repair
open_points.text: a stored status or waiting point that lags them ... is rewritten
open_points.question: Which change type and exact fields are used to rewrite each stale run before deciding whether it is running, and is ended_at changed?
options: one RecordRunProgressChange with no executions and fully rederived state
RecordResumptionChange followed by advance_run
no explicit rewrite; advance_run handles it
open_points.default_guess: Write one RecordRunProgressChange with no executions and the fully rederived status, outputs, waiting points, and terminal timestamp if applicable.

open_points.subject: recover_running_runs counting
open_points.text: Returns the number of runs advanced
open_points.question: Does the count include runs only repaired or re-reached, runs on which advance_run was called but made no change, or only calls made for runs left running?
options: count calls to advance_run
count every processed non-ended run
count only runs whose records changed
open_points.default_guess: Count each run for which advance_run is actually called.

open_points.subject: release_run
open_points.text: with released_at, then ... return derive_run_answer showing released_by and released_at
open_points.question: Is released_at one kernel_now value passed to the change, and must the Run be reread from record_change's result or via a new identity query?
options: take one timestamp and use record_change's returned Run
take one timestamp and reread by identity
derive by locally copying the old Run
open_points.default_guess: Take one kernel_now value and use the Run returned in the RecordSet from record_change.

open_points.subject: resume_run current inputs
open_points.text: reach again ... every element waiting with reason service_unreachable ... with its current inputs
open_points.question: How are current inputs reconstructed for mapped and unmapped elements, including transient mapped-element StoredValues and aggregate file references after restart?
options: rederive them from the pinned graph and trace
reuse the latest NodeExecution.inputs
reuse the latest EffectAttempt.inputs
open_points.default_guess: Reuse the latest waiting NodeExecution or EffectAttempt inputs for the exact element.

open_points.subject: resume_run partial resend
open_points.text: only after all those resends advance the run
open_points.question: If reaching one waiting element raises after earlier elements were resent, should the function stop immediately, continue the remaining resends, or still call advance_run?
options: stop immediately and propagate
continue all resends then propagate
advance before propagating
open_points.default_guess: Stop immediately and propagate.

open_points.subject: start_run supported input types
open_points.text: inputs: tuple[PortPayload, ...] ... each input ... a JsonCandidate of its canonical bytes ... publish each input's canonical bytes ... StoredValues of value carriage
open_points.question: Are file and file-list flow inputs permitted by PortPayload and Port.carriage, or are start_run inputs restricted to JSON value payloads?
options: only JsonPayload is permitted
all PortPayload variants are permitted and need carriage-specific handling
flow input ports are implicitly always value ports
open_points.default_guess: Restrict start_run to JsonPayload/value ports and refuse file inputs.

open_points.subject: start_run input disclosure
open_points.text: StoredValues ... size and class
open_points.question: What disclosure_class is assigned to each initial StoredValue when JsonPayload has no class and Port.disclosure_class is nullable?
options: use the port's disclosure_class and default null to open
always open
reject ports whose disclosure_class is null
open_points.default_guess: Use the port's disclosure_class, defaulting null to open.

open_points.subject: start_run identities
open_points.text: value_id and value_digest come from content_identity
open_points.question: Which IdentitySubject is passed for value_digest and which for value_id, and how is the StoredValueContent identity computed when it itself requires value_digest?
options: digest BytesContent for value_digest, then digest StoredValueContent for value_id
use put_value_bytes return value as digest, then content_identity for value_id
use one identity for both fields
open_points.default_guess: Compute value_digest from BytesContent, publish with that digest, then compute value_id from StoredValueContent.

open_points.subject: start_run run identity
open_points.text: write one StartRunChange ... Then MUST advance the run with advance_run
open_points.question: How is the newly created run_id obtained when StartRunChange has no run_id field and starts are explicitly never deduplicated?
options: record_change generates a Run and returns it
derive an identity using time or actor
the store provides an undocumented run-id generator
open_points.default_guess: Take the sole newly created Run from record_change's returned RecordSet.

open_points.subject: start_run activation consistency
open_points.text: one PinnedImplementation per function node with the implementation of that current activation
open_points.question: If current_activation changes between validation reads, which activation is pinned, and must all activations be read from one consistent store snapshot?
options: retain the Activation objects obtained during validation
reread immediately before StartRunChange
record_change detects stale activations
open_points.default_guess: Retain and pin the exact Activation objects read during validation.

open_points.subject: start_run publication failure
open_points.text: publish each input's canonical bytes with put_value_bytes, and write one StartRunChange
open_points.question: If publication or record_change fails partway, how are already published input blobs handled, and must no-run-on-failure include cleanup of those blobs?
options: leave unreachable content-addressed blobs
attempt cleanup through an unavailable API
the store guarantees transactionality across these calls
